question: Veda Samaj, the 'Brahmo Samaj of the South', was established in 1864 at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madras.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Veda Samaj, called the 'Brahmo Samaj of South', was founded at Madras in 1864 by Keshab Chandra Sen's follower K. Sridharalu Naidu and associates (वेद समाज, मद्रास 1864)

 

• It was inspired by the ideals of the Brahmo Samaj, rejecting caste and promoting monotheism and social reform.

 

• The Samaj was active in the Madras region and spread Brahmo ideas in the south.

 

• It reflects how the Bengal reform ideas travelled to other regions in the 1860s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sridharalu Naidu later translated Brahmo books into Tamil and Telugu.

 

• The Prarthana Samaj (1867) was the equivalent movement in western India.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen toured south India in 1864.

 

• The Madras reformers around Sridharalu Naidu translated Brahmo texts into Tamil and Telugu, and the Veda Samaj later became the Brahmo Samaj of South India. Keshab's tour of Madras in 1864 was the initial spark.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta (Option 1): Calcutta was the home of the parent Brahmo Samaj (1828) and the place where Keshab Chandra Sen was active, so the southern branch was by definition elsewhere.

 

• Bombay (Option 3): Bombay is the city of the Prarthana Samaj (1867) and Arya Samaj (1875); the Veda Samaj originated in the Tamil region and not in Maharashtra.

 

• Mysore (Option 4): Mysore was a princely state in the south, but the Veda Samaj was founded in the Madras Presidency's capital and not at Mysore.

question: Following the 1866 split in the Brahmo Samaj, the Adi Brahmo Samaj was led by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Debendranath Tagore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After the split the Adi Brahmo Samaj continued under Debendranath Tagore, father of Rabindranath Tagore, while Keshab Chandra Sen headed the Brahmo Samaj of India (आदि ब्रह्म समाज — देवेंद्रनाथ टैगोर)

 

• Debendranath carried on the work of Roy's society and revived it after taking charge.

 

• The division arose from Keshab's progressive stands such as support for inter-caste marriage and wider social changes, which the older group resisted.

 

• The Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 at Calcutta to purify Hinduism and preach monotheism.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Debendranath ran the Tattvabodhini Sabha (1839).

 

• A third split in 1878 created the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Keshab's Samaj spread branches to Bombay, Madras and the Punjab.

 

• The two Brahmo wings divided over Keshab's insistence on inter-caste marriage; a further split in 1878 produced the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj after Keshab married his minor daughter to the Maharaja of Cooch Behar.

 

NOTE

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 2): Keshab Chandra Sen headed the other side, the Brahmo Samaj of India, which broke away; he did not lead the conservative Adi Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Option 3): Raja Ram Mohan Roy had died in 1833, so he could not lead any group three decades later, though he is the founder of the original body.

 

• Atmaram Pandurang (Option 4): Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj at Bombay, a different organisation from the Calcutta Brahmo body, and had no role in its internal division.

question: The Sati abolition regulation of 1829 was passed under the Governor-Generalship of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord William Bentinck.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The practice of Sati was declared illegal in 1829 by Lord William Bentinck through Regulation XVII, after Roy's long campaign (सती प्रथा का उन्मूलन — विलियम बेंटिक, 1829)

 

• The measure first applied to the Bengal Presidency and was soon extended to the rest of British India.

 

• Roy's journals and pleas for scriptural reinterpretation had prepared public opinion in its favour.

 

• Bentinck's tenure also saw other reforms, including the suppression of Thuggee and the adoption of English as the medium of higher education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Orthodox groups in Calcutta formed the Dharma Sabha under Radhakanta Deb to protest.

 

• The Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 was passed under Canning.

 

• Female infanticide was banned in 1795 and 1804.

 

• Bentinck relied on Roy and on officials like Charles Metcalfe, and he also suppressed Thuggee under William Sleeman. His 1835 decision on English education followed Macaulay's Minute, within his term as Governor-General.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Cornwallis (Option 1): Lord Cornwallis, Governor-General in 1786-93 and 1805, is known for the Permanent Settlement and judicial reforms, not for abolishing Sati.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 3): Lord Dalhousie served in 1848-56 and is famed for the Doctrine of Lapse and railways; the Sati ban came nearly two decades earlier.

 

• Lord Canning (Option 4): Lord Canning was Governor-General at the time of the 1857 revolt and the Widow Remarriage Act, but the 1829 Sati measure had been enacted long before his term.

question:
Match the reformer (Column A) with the organisation or work (Column B):

Column A: (a) Raja Ram Mohan Roy (b) Dayanand Saraswati (c) Atmaram Pandurang (d) Jyotiba Phule

Column B: (i) Prarthana Samaj (ii) Satyashodak Samaj (iii) Brahmo Sabha (iv) Arya Samaj
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roy started the Brahmo Sabha in August 1828, Dayanand the Arya Samaj (1875), Atmaram Pandurang the Prarthana Samaj (1867) and Phule the Satyashodak Samaj (1873) (सही मिलान: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii)

 

• Pair (a)-(iii): the Brahmo Sabha of 1828 at Calcutta later became the Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Pair (b)-(iv): Dayanand's Arya Samaj was set up at Bombay and stood for Vedic revival.

 

• Pair (c)-(i): the Prarthana Samaj was an off-shoot of the Brahmo Samaj in Bombay; Pair (d)-(ii): Phule's Samaj opposed Brahmanical domination in Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Debendranath Tagore revived Roy's Brahmo Samaj, while Ranade and Bhandarkar later strengthened the Prarthana Samaj.

 

• Arya Samaj: 1875; Prarthana Samaj: 1867; Satyashodak Samaj: 1873 gives a neat chronological order.

 

• All four bodies belong to the period between 1828 and 1875.

 

• The Brahmo Samaj was formed in Calcutta in 1828, Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875, Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867 and Satyashodak Samaj in Poona in 1873. Three of the four were founded in Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii (Option 2): This set swaps Roy and Dayanand: it gives Roy the Arya Samaj, a Bombay body of 1875 formed long after his death, and gives Dayanand the Brahmo Sabha of 1828.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 3): This set reverses the last two pairs, treating Atmaram Pandurang as the founder of the Satyashodak Samaj and Phule as the Prarthana Samaj's founder, though they belong respectively to Bombay and Poona traditions.

 

• a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii (Option 4): This set gives the Prarthana Samaj to Roy and the Brahmo Sabha to Atmaram Pandurang, which reverses their real founders; Roy's Brahmo body of 1828 preceded the Bombay society by almost four decades.

question:
Match the movement/organisation (Column A) with the year of its founding (Column B):

Column A: (a) Atmiya Sabha (b) Prarthana Samaj (c) Satyashodak Samaj (d) Ramakrishna Mission

Column B: (i) 1815 (ii) 1867 (iii) 1873 (iv) 1897
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Atmiya Sabha was begun by Roy in 1815; Prarthana Samaj in 1867; Satyashodak Samaj in 1873; Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 (सही मिलान: a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv)

 

• (a) The Atmiya Sabha was Roy's first organisation, preceding his Brahmo Sabha of 1828.

 

• (b) The Prarthana Samaj was founded at Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang.

 

• (c) Phule's Satyashodak Samaj came in 1873, the year of his Gulamgiri; (d) Vivekananda set up the Mission in 1897 at Belur Math.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The years form an ascending series, so a chronological arrangement matches the right answer.

 

• Vivekananda established the Mission after his return from the West, in memory of his Guru.

 

• The Arya Samaj (1875) and Theosophical Society (1875) fall between Satyashodak and the Mission.

 

• Gulamgiri in the same year as the Satyashodak Samaj carried the dedication to American supporters of the abolition of slavery. The Atmiya Sabha of 1815 is the oldest among these four organisations.

 

NOTE

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv (Option 1): This combination exchanges Prarthana Samaj and Atmiya Sabha, making the Bombay Samaj the earliest although the Atmiya Sabha of Calcutta predates it by fifty-two years.

 

• a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv (Option 2): This combination puts the Satyashodak Samaj in 1867 and the Prarthana Samaj in 1873, interchanging the two Maharashtra bodies which in fact arose in 1873 and 1867 respectively.

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii (Option 4): This combination swaps the Satyashodak Samaj with the Ramakrishna Mission, dating Phule's society to 1897, though Phule died in 1890, a few years before that date.

question:
Match the person (Column A) with the book or journal (Column B):

Column A: (a) Dayanand Saraswati (b) Jyotiba Phule (c) Raja Ram Mohan Roy (d) Sir Syed Ahmad Khan

Column B: (i) Gulamgiri (ii) Satyarth Prakash (iii) Samvad Kaumudi (iv) Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dayanand wrote Satyarth Prakash, Phule wrote Gulamgiri, Roy edited Samvad Kaumudi, and Sir Syed ran Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq (सही मिलान: a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv)

 

• (a) Satyarth Prakash (1875) is called the Bible of the Arya Samaj.

 

• (b) Gulamgiri (1873) attacked Brahmin supremacy and caste slavery.

 

• (c) Samvad Kaumudi was Roy's Bengali weekly; (d) Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was Syed's journal for social reform among Muslims.

 

• The pairing logic is useful: each of the four works expresses the main concern of its author, whether Vedic revival, caste critique, press-based reform or Muslim modernisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roy also edited the Persian weekly Mirat-ul-Akhbar.

 

• Phule's Sarvajanik Satya Dharma Pustak was published posthumously.

 

• Sir Syed's journal was started in 1870 and was also known as the Mohammedan Social Reformer.

 

• Sir Syed's journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was published from 1870 under the English name Mohammedan Social Reformer. Gulamgiri was written in Marathi, while Satyarth Prakash was composed in Hindi for common readers.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv (Option 1): This version gives Gulamgiri to Dayanand and Satyarth Prakash to Phule, which is the wrong way round, as Satyarth Prakash is the central text of the Arya Samaj.

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii (Option 2): This version attributes Samvad Kaumudi to Sir Syed and Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq to Roy, swapping a Bengali weekly of the 1820s with an 1870 Aligarh journal.

 

• a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i (Option 3): This version assigns Samvad Kaumudi to Dayanand and Gulamgiri to Sir Syed, so every pair mismatches the author of the work.

question:
Match the reformer (Column A) with the place or institution associated with him/her (Column B):

Column A: (a) Henry Vivian Derozio (b) Annie Besant (c) Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (d) Lala Lajpat Rai

Column B: (i) Hindu College, Calcutta (ii) Central Hindu School, Banaras (iii) Aligarh (iv) DAV institutions, Lahore
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Derozio taught at Hindu College, Annie Besant founded the Central Hindu School at Banaras, Sir Syed built the college at Aligarh, and Lajpat Rai worked for the DAV institutions at Lahore (सही मिलान: a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv)

 

• (a) Derozio inspired the Young Bengal group among his students at Hindu College.

 

• (b) Besant's school of 1898 later became the nucleus of Banaras Hindu University.

 

• (c) The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College (1875) became AMU; (d) Lajpat Rai was an Arya Samaj leader associated with DAV.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hindu College was set up in Calcutta in 1817 with David Hare and Roy's help.

 

• The first DAV school was opened at Lahore in 1886.

 

• Besant came to India in 1893 and led the Theosophical Society from 1907.

 

• Hindu College of 1817 became Presidency College after 1855. The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College opened at Aligarh in 1875 and was granted university status in 1920 as Aligarh Muslim University.

 

NOTE

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv (Option 2): This option exchanges Derozio's and Besant's institutions, placing the Young Bengal teacher in Banaras and the Theosophist in Calcutta, which reverses their true associations.

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii (Option 3): This option exchanges Sir Syed's Aligarh and Lajpat Rai's Lahore, giving the Muslim educationist the DAV schools and the Punjab leader the Muslim college.

 

• a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv (Option 4): This option gives Derozio to Aligarh and Besant to Hindu College, Calcutta, and Sir Syed to the Banaras school, so three of four pairs fail.

question:
Match the movement (Column A) with its leader or key figure (Column B):

Column A: (a) Self-Respect Movement (b) Aligarh Movement (c) Veda Samaj (d) Young Bengal Movement

Column B: (i) Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (ii) E.V. Ramasamy Periyar (iii) K. Sridharalu Naidu (iv) H.V. Derozio
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Self-Respect Movement (1925) was led by Periyar, the Aligarh Movement by Sir Syed, the Veda Samaj (1864) by K. Sridharalu Naidu and Young Bengal by Derozio (सही मिलान: a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv)

 

• (a) Periyar's movement uplifted Dravidians against Brahminical tyranny.

 

• (b) Sir Syed worked for the educational advancement of Muslims.

 

• (c) Veda Samaj was the Brahmo Samaj of the South; (d) Derozio taught at Hindu College and inspired radical students.

 

• Together the pairs show a spread across regions: Tamil Nadu, the North-Western Provinces, Madras and Bengal, each with its own leader and focus of reform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Self-Respect Movement began in 1925, Aligarh college in 1875, Veda Samaj 1864 and Young Bengal in the 1820s-30s.

 

• Naidu worked with Keshab Chandra Sen's ideas.

 

• Periyar's later body was the Dravidar Kazhagam.

 

• The Veda Samaj took its name from Vedic scripture, though it followed the Brahmo model of theism without rituals. The Dravidar Kazhagam of 1944 emerged from the Self-Respect Movement under Periyar.

 

NOTE

 

• a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv (Option 1): This option swaps Periyar and Sir Syed, crediting the Muslim educationist with the Tamil Self-Respect Movement and the Dravidian leader with the Aligarh Movement.

 

• a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii (Option 3): This option swaps the Veda Samaj with Young Bengal's leader, so it gives Naidu to the Derozio circle and Derozio to the Samaj, which is a clear mismatch of regions.

 

• a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv (Option 4): This option links the Self-Respect Movement with Naidu, Aligarh with Periyar and the Veda Samaj with Sir Syed, none of which has any historical basis.

question:
Arrange the following in chronological order:

(a) Founding of the Brahmo Sabha (b) Abolition of Sati (c) Widow Remarriage Act (d) Founding of the Prarthana Samaj
solution_text:
The correct answer is a, b, c, d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Order: Brahmo Sabha (1828), abolition of Sati (1829), Widow Remarriage Act (1856), Prarthana Samaj (1867) (कालक्रम: ब्रह्म सभा, सती उन्मूलन, विधवा पुनर्विवाह, प्रार्थना समाज)

 

• Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in August 1828, and Bentinck's Regulation XVII banned Sati the following year.

 

• The Widow Remarriage Act (1856) followed Vidyasagar's efforts in Bengal.

 

• Atmaram Pandurang launched the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867.

 

• The first two events took place within two years of each other under Roy's influence, while the other two belong to the middle decades of the century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sati abolition came under Bentinck, widow remarriage under Canning's term.

 

• Roy's Atmiya Sabha (1815) came even before these events.

 

• The Arya Samaj followed in 1875.

 

• The Brahmo Sabha was transformed into the Brahmo Samaj when its own building opened in January 1830. Lord Canning's Governor-Generalship covered the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 and the revolt of 1857.

 

NOTE

 

• b, a, c, d (Option 2): Putting Sati abolition ahead of the Brahmo Sabha reverses 1828 and 1829; the Sabha was started a year before the regulation.

 

• a, c, b, d (Option 3): Placing the widow remarriage law before the abolition of Sati is incorrect since the 1856 Act came twenty-seven years after the 1829 regulation.

 

• a, b, d, c (Option 4): Ending with the widow remarriage law after the Prarthana Samaj is wrong because 1856 precedes the 1867 founding of the Bombay Samaj.

question:
Arrange the following in chronological order of founding:

(a) Veda Samaj (b) Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam (c) Prarthana Samaj (d) Satyashodak Samaj
solution_text:
The correct answer is a, b, c, d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Order: Veda Samaj (1864), Samarasa Suddha Sanmarga Sangam (1865), Prarthana Samaj (1867), Satyashodak Samaj (1873) (कालक्रम: वेद समाज 1864, संगम 1865, प्रार्थना 1867, सत्यशोधक 1873)

 

• The Veda Samaj was started at Madras under the Brahmo influence in 1864.

 

• Ramalinga's casteless society followed in 1865.

 

• Bombay's Prarthana Samaj (1867) preceded Phule's Poona-based Samaj of 1873.

 

• The sequence shows reform ideas spreading from Madras in 1864 to Bombay in 1867, and later to Poona in 1873, before the end of the 1870s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• South India saw two reform bodies in these years.

 

• Ranade joined the Prarthana Samaj in 1870.

 

• Gulamgiri was published in 1873 alongside the Satyashodak Samaj.

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen visited Madras and Bombay in 1864, which stirred the creation of both the Veda Samaj and the Prarthana Samaj. These were regional echoes of the Bengal-based Brahmo Samaj.

 

NOTE

 

• b, a, c, d (Option 1): Starting with Ramalinga's Sangam reverses the first two dates, since the Veda Samaj was started in 1864, a year before the Sangam's founding in 1865.

 

• a, c, b, d (Option 2): Starting with the Prarthana Samaj or any order that moves the Bombay body ahead of Ramalinga's Sangam fails, because 1867 comes after 1865 and the Sangam therefore belongs earlier in the sequence.

 

• a, b, d, c (Option 3): Putting the Prarthana Samaj last after the Satyashodak Samaj reverses 1867 and 1873, though the Bombay Samaj was the earlier of the two.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

(a) Opening of the first girls' school at Poona (b) Foundation of the first Singh Sabha (c) Foundation of Khalsa College, Amritsar (d) Start of the Self-Respect Movement
solution_text:
The correct answer is a, b, c, d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Order: girls' school at Poona (1848), first Singh Sabha (1873), Khalsa College (1892), Self-Respect Movement (1925) (कालक्रम: 1848, 1873, 1892, 1925)

 

• The Phules opened the Poona girls' school in 1848.

 

• The Singh Sabha was formed at Amritsar in 1873, and its leaders founded the Khalsa College there in 1892.

 

• Periyar launched his movement in 1925 in Tamil Nadu.

 

• The four events cover almost eight decades, from the earliest girls' school to the arrival of the Dravidian rationalist movement in the twentieth century.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Savitribai taught at the school she co-founded with Jyotiba.

 

• The Chief Khalsa Diwan came in 1902.

 

• The Dravidar Kazhagam followed in 1944.

 

• Khalsa College was later given affiliation to Punjab University, and the Periyar-led movement took the form of a political party in 1944. The Chief Khalsa Diwan of 1902 coordinated Sikh institutions.

 

NOTE

 

• b, a, c, d (Option 1): Placing the Singh Sabha ahead of the Poona school puts 1873 before 1848, whereas the girls' school at Poona is the earliest of the four events and opened a quarter-century before.

 

• a, c, b, d (Option 2): Putting the Khalsa College before the first Singh Sabha is wrong because the college was a product of the Sabha movement established nineteen years after its start.

 

• a, b, d, c (Option 4): Placing the Khalsa College ahead of the Singh Sabha mistakes cause for effect, since the college of 1892 was created by leaders of a movement that had already started in 1873.

question:
Consider the following statements about Jyotiba Phule:

1. He founded the Satyashodak Samaj in 1873.

2. He wrote Gulamgiri.

3. He started the first girls' school at Poona with his wife in 1848.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements hold: Phule founded the Satyashodak Samaj (1873), authored Gulamgiri and opened the Poona girls' school in 1848 with Savitribai (तीनों कथन सही हैं — ज्योतिबा फुले)

 

• Gulamgiri (1873) exposed caste oppression and Brahmanical domination.

 

• The girls' school helped to make him a symbol of women's education.

 

• He was born in a low-caste family in Maharashtra and fought upper-caste domination throughout his life.

 

• The three statements together describe his work in education, literature and organisation, which is why he is remembered as a pioneer of the anti-caste movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Phule pioneered the widow remarriage movement in Maharashtra.

 

• He is called the first feminist, as is his wife by some accounts.

 

• He died in 1890.

 

• Phule and his wife also opened a home for new-born children of widows and an orphanage. He died on 28 November 1890, and the Satyashodak Samaj later spread among non-Brahmin groups of Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Leaving out statement 3 is wrong because Phule and his wife Savitribai really did open the first girls' school at Poona in 1848, which is among his best-known achievements in education.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 3): Leaving out statement 1 is wrong because Phule himself founded the Satyashodak Samaj in 1873, the organisation through which he fought caste domination and Brahmin ritual supremacy in Maharashtra.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 4): Leaving out statement 2 is wrong because Gulamgiri, a Marathi book written in 1873 that compared caste slavery with slavery in America, was authored by Phule and was not written by anyone else.

question:
Assertion (A): The Arya Samaj opposed idol worship.

Reason (R): Dayanand Saraswati regarded the Vedas as the source of true knowledge and gave the call 'Back to the Vedas'.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: A is false but R is true
option_4: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Both statements are true and linked: since Dayanand held the Vedas as the fountain of true knowledge, he rejected later practices like idol worship, child marriage and caste by birth (दोनों सही, R, A की सही व्याख्या)

 

• His call 'Back to the Vedas' meant discarding post-Vedic ritual accretions in favour of the pure monotheism he found in the Vedic hymns.

 

• The Arya Samaj therefore promoted Vedic ritual, havan and education while condemning image worship.

 

• The same Vedic outlook underlies its stand on equality of men and women.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The movement was founded at Bombay in 1875.

 

• Dayanand's Satyarth Prakash elaborates his arguments against idolatry.

 

• He also began the Suddhi movement.

 

• Dayanand rejected the authority of the Puranas and the Brahmin priesthood, explaining that the Vedas teach one formless God. Arya Samajis perform the havan, and the Samaj's ten principles were framed in 1877 at Lahore.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): The reason does not merely coexist with the assertion; it is the cause of it, because the Samaj's anti-idol stance arose directly from its Vedic orientation, so the 'not the correct explanation' choice is untenable.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): Calling the reason false is incorrect; Dayanand did treat the Vedas as the source of true knowledge and used 'Back to the Vedas' as his motto.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 3): Calling the assertion false is wrong, since the Arya Samaj opposed idol worship alongside child marriage, untouchability and caste by birth, as part of its basic reformist programme from 1875.

question:
Assertion (A): Swami Vivekananda raised the prestige of India and Hinduism abroad.

Reason (R): He attended the Parliament of the World's Religions at Chicago in 1893.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true but R is false
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vivekananda's appearance at the Chicago Parliament of Religions in September 1893 directly gave Hinduism a respected place before a global audience, so the reason explains the assertion (दोनों कथन सही; R, A की व्याख्या)

 

• His speeches presented Vedanta's universality and tolerance.

 

• The success earned him lecture invitations in the United States and England, and recruits for his later work.

 

• On return he established the Ramakrishna Mission (1897) at Belur Math in memory of his Guru Ramakrishna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• His original name was Narendra Nath Dutt (1863-1902).

 

• He taught the idea of service to the poor as worship of God.

 

• Sister Nivedita was among his Western disciples.

 

• Vivekananda's philosophy was neo-Vedanta, teaching the divinity of the soul and the unity of all religions. He is commemorated on 12 January, his birthday, which is observed as National Youth Day in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 2): Saying the reason is true but not the explanation fails, because the Chicago speeches were the very occasion through which India's and Hinduism's image was uplifted abroad.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 3): Treating the reason as false is incorrect, since Vivekananda really did attend the Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): Treating the assertion as false is incorrect; his Chicago address is remembered precisely for raising the prestige of India and Hinduism in the West.

question:
Assertion (A): The headquarters of the Theosophical Society in India is at Adyar, Madras.

Reason (R): The Society was founded in Calcutta in 1875 by Dayanand Saraswati and Annie Besant.
option_1: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is A is true but R is false.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The assertion is true: the Society established its headquarters at Adyar, Madras in 1882; the reason is false, because it was founded in New York in 1875 by Blavatsky and Olcott (A सही, R गलत)

 

• Dayanand Saraswati had no connection with the Society's founding; he founded the Arya Samaj, a purely Indian movement.

 

• Annie Besant arrived in India only in 1893 and succeeded Olcott as head after 1907.

 

• Thus the facts in R are wrong in place, year and persons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besant was a British Theosophist and Irish-born social campaigner.

 

• The Society's aims included universal brotherhood and the study of ancient religions.

 

• Madame Blavatsky came from Russia; Olcott was an American colonel.

 

• Colonel Olcott also helped found Buddhist schools in Ceylon. The Theosophical Society's Adyar library holds many ancient manuscripts, and Adyar remains the international headquarters of the Society to this day.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A (Option 1): The two statements cannot both be true; the founding of the Society in Calcutta by Dayanand and Besant is incorrect, so no explanation can be built on it.

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 3): Even apart from explanation, the reason misstates the founders and venue, so the claim that both are true with R as a non-explanation is invalid.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): The assertion is certainly valid, as Adyar is the Theosophical headquarters since 1882, so saying A is false while R is true gets both statements wrong.

question:
Assertion (A): The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College was founded at Aligarh by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan.

Reason (R): Sir Syed wished to promote English education among Muslims.
option_1: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_2: A is true but R is false
option_3: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
option_4: A is false but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The college set up in 1875 at Aligarh was intended to bring modern English education to Muslims, so R explains A (दोनों सही; R, A की सही व्याख्या)

 

• Sir Syed (1817-98) believed that the community's advancement depended on Western science and learning combined with a rational reading of Islam.

 

• His effort, the Aligarh Movement, aimed at the social and educational advancement of Muslims.

 

• The college later grew into the Aligarh Muslim University.

 

• Because the reason states the purpose of the college, the assertion and reason form a cause-and-effect pair, with English education being the college's central objective.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sir Syed discouraged Muslims from joining the Congress, founded in 1885.

 

• His journal Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq spread social reform ideas.

 

• AMU became a Central university in 1920.

 

• Sir Syed's faith in loyalty to the British and Western science separated him from the Congress, which he criticised in the 1880s. He also founded the United Patriotic Association in 1888 together with Raja Shiv Prasad.

 

NOTE

 

• Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A (Option 1): Denying that the reason explains the assertion is wrong, because the college existed for the purpose stated in the reason.

 

• A is true but R is false (Option 2): The reason is not false: promoting English education among Muslims was the central object of both the college and the Aligarh Movement.

 

• A is false but R is true (Option 4): The assertion is not false: Aligarh's Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College was indeed founded by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan in 1875.

question: Which of the following is NOT associated with Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satyashodak Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Satyashodak Samaj (1873) was created by Jyotiba Phule to fight caste domination; it has no link with Roy, who died in 1833 (सत्यशोधक समाज फुले का था, रॉय का नहीं)

 

• The Atmiya Sabha (1815) was Roy's first society for discussing monotheism and reform.

 

• Samvad Kaumudi was his Bengali weekly, used in the anti-Sati campaign.

 

• The Brahmo Sabha (August 1828) evolved into the Brahmo Samaj, which Debendranath Tagore later led.

 

• The answer depends on remembering that the Satyashodak Samaj belongs to Maharashtra and to Jyotiba Phule, not to Bengal's Roy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Roy also edited the Persian weekly Mirat-ul-Akhbar.

 

• He helped David Hare establish Hindu College.

 

• Phule's Samaj aimed at lower-caste empowerment in Maharashtra.

 

• Roy's friends Dwarkanath Tagore and Prasanna Kumar Tagore supported his institutions. Phule's Samaj, on the other hand, operated in Maharashtra and was set up forty years after Roy's death in 1833.

 

NOTE

 

• Atmiya Sabha (Option 1): The Atmiya Sabha was founded by Roy in 1815 to propagate monotheism and attack idolatry, so it is genuinely associated with him and cannot be the answer to a NOT question.

 

• Samvad Kaumudi (Option 3): Samvad Kaumudi is the first Bengali weekly started by Roy; being definitely his journal, it is not the exception asked for.

 

• Brahmo Sabha (Option 4): The Brahmo Sabha of 1828 was established by Roy and became the Brahmo Samaj, so it too is associated with him.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Periyar - Satyashodak Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Satyashodak Samaj belongs to Jyotiba Phule (1873); Periyar is linked with the Self-Respect Movement (1925), so this pair is wrong (पेरियार - आत्म-सम्मान आंदोलन, सत्यशोधक नहीं)

 

• Dayanand began the Suddhi movement to bring back converts.

 

• Vidyasagar's campaign culminated in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.

 

• Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay in 1867.

 

• The incorrect pair mixes a Tamil rationalist figure with a Maharashtra anti-caste society, two movements separated by region and by over fifty years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Periyar's Self-Respect Movement aimed at exposing Brahminical dominance in Tamil society.

 

• Phule's Gulamgiri is dated 1873.

 

• Ranade and Bhandarkar joined the Prarthana Samaj in 1870.

 

• Periyar's Self-Respect Movement is distinct from the Justice Party, which sought non-Brahmin representation in the Madras Presidency from 1916. Phule's Samaj was nearly fifty years older than Periyar's movement.

 

NOTE

 

• Dayanand Saraswati - Suddhi movement (Option 1): The Suddhi link is correct, as Dayanand started this reconversion movement; being correct, it cannot be the answer to a question seeking the incorrect pair.

 

• Vidyasagar - Widow Remarriage Act (1856) (Option 2): Vidyasagar and the 1856 Act form a valid pair because his advocacy of widow remarriage led to its passage, so it is not the odd one out.

 

• Atmaram Pandurang - Prarthana Samaj (Option 3): Atmaram Pandurang is rightly paired with the Prarthana Samaj of 1867, so this pair is correct and therefore not the exception.

question: Which of the following was NOT an objective or feature of the Arya Samaj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Promoting idol worship.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arya Samaj opposed idol worship, so promoting it is not a feature; the movement rested on Vedic monotheism (मूर्ति पूजा का समर्थन आर्य समाज का लक्ष्य नहीं था)

 

• It supported widow remarriage, equal rights for men and women, and inter-caste marriage.

 

• It opposed untouchability, child marriage and caste discrimination.

 

• It promoted women's education and built DAV institutions, the first DAV school opening at Lahore in 1886.

 

• Its social programme was therefore reformist and egalitarian, yet strictly Vedic in religion: rituals were reduced to the havan, and temples and images were discarded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dayanand's Satyarth Prakash (1875) expounds these ideas.

 

• He campaigned for 'Back to the Vedas'.

 

• The Samaj was set up in Bombay.

 

• The Arya Samaj preached the ten principles that emphasise truth, knowledge of the Vedas and service to the world. The movement was strongest in Punjab, Delhi and the United Provinces rather than in the south.

 

NOTE

 

• Supporting widow remarriage (Option 2): Supporting widow remarriage was part of the Samaj's social programme, hence it is a genuine feature and not the exception.

 

• Opposing untouchability (Option 3): Opposition to untouchability and caste discrimination was explicitly part of its reformist agenda, so this cannot be the item that was not a feature.

 

• Encouraging women's education (Option 4): Encouraging women's education was a real aim of the Samaj and was carried out through girls' schools and the DAV network.

question: Hindu College, Calcutta, where Derozio taught, was founded in 1817 with the help of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and:
solution_text:
The correct answer is David Hare.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hindu College was established in Calcutta in 1817 with David Hare, a Scottish watchmaker and educationist, and Roy assisted him (डेविड हेयर — हिंदू कॉलेज, कलकत्ता)

 

• The college offered Western education to Indian students and later became Presidency College.

 

• Henry Vivian Derozio, teaching there, inspired the Young Bengal movement of radical thinkers.

 

• It thus links two strands of Bengal's reform, Roy's moderate and Derozio's radical.

 

• David Hare is also remembered for starting the School Society and helping to establish the Calcutta Medical College in the 1830s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sanskrit College at Banaras was founded in 1791 by Jonathan Duncan.

 

• Calcutta Madrasa was set up in 1781 by Warren Hastings.

 

• Macaulay's Minute (1835) advocated English education.

 

• David Hare was a Scottish watchmaker who devoted his life to Indian education and also set up the School Society in 1818. Hindu College's teachers included Derozio, who joined in 1828 as a lecturer.

 

NOTE

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 1): Warren Hastings founded the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781, an institution for Persian and Arabic learning, and was not involved in the Hindu College set up decades later.

 

• Jonathan Duncan (Option 3): Jonathan Duncan, Resident at Banaras, founded the Sanskrit College there in 1791; he is not linked with Hindu College of Calcutta.

 

• T.B. Macaulay (Option 4): Macaulay's Minute of 1835 supported English as the medium of education, but he came to India after Hindu College existed and was not its co-founder.

question:
Consider the following statements about Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and the Aligarh Movement:

1. Sir Syed lived from 1817 to 1898.

2. The Aligarh college was founded in 1875.

3. The college later grew into the Aligarh Muslim University.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are accurate: Sir Syed lived 1817-98, founded the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875, and it later became Aligarh Muslim University (सभी तीनों कथन सही)

 

• The Aligarh Movement aimed at the social and educational advancement of Muslims.

 

• Teaching English and Western science alongside religious studies was central to its approach.

 

• The institution attracted students from across India and became a hub of Muslim intellectual life.

 

• The three statements concern birth years, the founding date and the later status of the college, so all of them are factual.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The title Sir was conferred by the British in 1888.

 

• Sir Syed wrote Asbab-e-Baghawat-e-Hind on the 1857 revolt.

 

• AMU received its charter in 1920.

 

• The Aligarh Movement's leaders included Mohsin-ul-Mulk and Altaf Hussain Hali. The Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College was modelled on Oxford and Cambridge, which Syed Ahmad had visited in England during 1869-70.

 

NOTE

 

• 1 and 2 only (Option 1): Leaving out statement 3 is wrong because the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College did later grow into Aligarh Muslim University, which received its university status by an Act of 1920 and continues today.

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 2): Leaving out statement 1 is wrong because Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was born in 1817 and died in 1898, so the span given in the statement is correct for the founder of the Aligarh Movement.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 3): Leaving out statement 2 is wrong because the Mohammedan Anglo Oriental College was founded at Aligarh in 1875, which was the foundation year of the institution that became a leading Muslim university.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Theosophical Society and Annie Besant:

1. The Society's headquarters was shifted to Adyar in 1882.

2. Annie Besant took over the leadership after Olcott's death in 1907.

3. Annie Besant founded the Dayanand Anglo-Vedic School at Lahore.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 only.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the headquarters was established at Adyar in 1882, and Annie Besant, in India since 1893, led the Society after Olcott's death in 1907 (कथन 1 और 2 सही)

 

• Statement 3 is wrong: the DAV institutions were started by the Arya Samaj at Lahore (first school 1886).

 

• Besant's own educational contribution was the Central Hindu School, Banaras (1898).

 

• The Society's objective included universal brotherhood without distinction of race, colour or creed.

 

• The Society also published books on Hindu and Buddhist philosophy and kept an international library, and Besant was both Theosophical president and an active political leader.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besant later started the Home Rule League (1916).

 

• She presided over the 1917 Calcutta Congress session.

 

• Madame Blavatsky and Olcott founded the Society in 1875.

 

• Mrs Besant presided over the Calcutta session of the Congress in 1917 and had earlier launched the Home Rule League at Madras in September 1916. The Theosophical Society's seat remains at Adyar, Chennai.

 

NOTE

 

• 2 and 3 only (Option 1): Pairing statements 2 and 3 acknowledges Besant's leadership but credits her with a DAV school, which belonged to the Arya Samaj; it also omits the true Adyar fact.

 

• 1 and 3 only (Option 2): Pairing statements 1 and 3 includes the wrong credit of the DAV school to Besant; both Besant and the Society had separate aims from the Arya Samaj.

 

• 1, 2 and 3 (Option 4): Including all three is wrong since the third statement confuses Besant's Central Hindu School at Banaras with the Arya Samaj's Lahore schools.

question: Which reform organisation is correctly paired with its founding city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj - Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arya Samaj was established at Bombay in 1875 by Dayanand Saraswati, so this is the only correct pair (आर्य समाज — बंबई, 1875)

 

• The Brahmo Samaj began in Calcutta (1828) and had a southern offshoot, the Veda Samaj, at Madras.

 

• The Prarthana Samaj was set up in Bombay in 1867.

 

• The Satyashodak Samaj (1873) was founded in the Poona region of Maharashtra by Phule.

 

• Among the options, only one gives the city where a movement was actually founded; the others shift Brahmo, Prarthana and Satyashodak bodies to unrelated cities.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arya Samaj later made Lahore its main stronghold.

 

• The Theosophical Society, by contrast, started in New York.

 

• Singh Sabha began in Amritsar.

 

• The Arya Samaj later grew to be strongest in Lahore, whereas the Prarthana Samaj had its base in Bombay and Pune. Veda Samaj, the Brahmo counterpart, operated in Madras. Thus the Bombay Presidency saw several movements.

 

NOTE

 

• Brahmo Samaj - Madras (Option 1): Madras is the home of the Veda Samaj, the southern counterpart of the Brahmo body, but the Brahmo Samaj itself was formed in Calcutta by Roy in 1828.

 

• Prarthana Samaj - Lahore (Option 3): Lahore was where the Arya Samaj later had its largest following and where DAV schools were opened; the Prarthana Samaj originated in Bombay.

 

• Satyashodak Samaj - Calcutta (Option 4): Calcutta hosted the Brahmo movement and Young Bengal; the Satyashodak Samaj was a Maharashtrian movement, so it does not originate there.

question: The title 'Father of the Indian Renaissance' is usually given to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy, born at Radhanagar in Hooghly and died in 1833, is called the Father of the Indian Renaissance and the Bridge between the Future and the Past (राजा राममोहन राय — भारतीय पुनर्जागरण के जनक)

 

• He is also known as the Father of Modern India and the Father of Bengal Renaissance.

 

• His work combined criticism of social evils like Sati with the promotion of modern education and a free press.

 

• He stood for monotheism and rational interpretation of scripture, and did not accept the supremacy of Brahmin priests.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• He founded the Atmiya Sabha (1815) and the Brahmo Sabha (1828).

 

• He died at Bristol, England, in 1833.

 

• Sati abolition in 1829 owed much to his agitation.

 

• Roy introduced English, mathematics and science through Vedanta College (1825) and, in his 1823 letter to Lord Amherst, opposed the plan of a Sanskrit college in favour of Western sciences.

 

NOTE

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 2): Dayanand Saraswati is known for the Arya Samaj and the call 'Back to the Vedas'; he is a revivalist, and not the pioneer who started the nineteenth-century awakening.

 

• Sir Syed Ahmad Khan (Option 3): Sir Syed Ahmad Khan is remembered as the leader of Muslim educational modernisation at Aligarh, so he does not hold the title linked to the general Indian renaissance.

 

• Jyotiba Phule (Option 4): Jyotiba Phule is known as a social reformer and champion of the anti-caste movement in Maharashtra, but he is not the figure given this honorific title.

question: Which Persian weekly was edited by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mirat-ul-Akhbar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roy edited the Persian weekly Mirat-ul-Akhbar, in addition to starting the Bengali weekly Samvad Kaumudi, and thus used both languages to reach readers (मिरात-उल-अख़बार — रॉय का फ़ारसी साप्ताहिक)

 

• Persian was still the court and administrative language of Bengal in the early 1820s, so a Persian paper reached officials and the Muslim gentry.

 

• He protested in 1823 against the restrictive Press Regulation, defending the freedom of the press.

 

• His journals were used for propagating reform on Sati and for discussing religion and politics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• He is also called the Father of Modern India.

 

• Roy visited England as envoy of Akbar II and died at Bristol in 1833.

 

• His Brahmo Sabha was started in August 1828.

 

• Roy wrote 'Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin' in Persian (1803-04), a tract against idolatry and superstition among many religions. He used Persian as well as English and Bengali to widen his audience.

 

NOTE

 

• Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq (Option 1): Tahzib-ul-Akhlaq was a journal launched in 1870 by Sir Syed Ahmad Khan to spread social reform among Muslims; it came decades after Roy's death.

 

• Mooknayak (Option 2): Mooknayak was a Marathi periodical started in 1920 by B.R. Ambedkar to voice the grievances of the depressed classes; it is unrelated to Roy and belongs to a much later period.

 

• Somprakash (Option 3): Somprakash was a Bengali weekly started in 1858 under Dwarkanath Vidyabhushan, associated with the Vidyasagar circle, so it is not a Persian paper edited by Roy.
